To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose to represent each building block of robot system design as a differentiable neural network and apply it to a partially observable navigation task, where a robot must navigate to an unknown goal in an unknown environment.

(1) we propose a novel approach to integrate algorithmic planning and machine learning in a principaled manner and (2) we apply the proposed approach for a challenging partially observable navigation problem and successfully train navigation networks to solve this problem.

(i) NavNet can solve challenging, partially observable navigation tasks; (ii) NavNet can learn to use the 2-D floor maps for state estimation; (iii) NavNet can generalize to new environments; (iv) NavNet can be trained using only visual observations and the 2-D map, without the need for any other sensor data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following research question: How can we design a robot system that is capable of solving a challenging task in a previously unseen environment, without any prior knowledge of that environment, and only relying on a small amount of data collected during operation?
the design of novel robot system architectures for solving challenging tasks in real-world environments.
the following questions: 1. How to integrate deep learning with algorithmic planning in a principled and effective manner for robot control tasks.
